name: Screen candidate categories and products for demand and fit
what: Take a proposed product or category and run it through a fast pass of demand, competition and store-model checks before any research time is spent on it. Kills weak candidates early and stops founder taste from deciding alone.
encompasses: Check the category is large and existing, not invented
Scan for a sea of sameness and look for a felt problem or passionate community
Ground each pain point in a specific review, not a category-wide guess
Match the category to the revenue model wanted (repeat, subscription, one-off)
Screen for products scarce offline and absent from big retail
Score customization requests against what fulfilment can actually handle
Screen a marketplace listing candidate against that marketplace's own density and fees
Run every trend-tool idea through the same demand and margin checks
Log a pass, caution or reject with the reason
inputs: web: category search volume and trend tools
brand brain: category and product history (once built)
outputs: screened candidate list with pass/caution/reject and reason
founder_sees: A one-page pass/caution/reject verdict on each candidate product, with the reason.

name: Validate demand on video-commerce and social-native platforms
what: Check a candidate's demand signal on TikTok-style shop data and native ad feeds before trusting it, because a single viral clip or one platform's number is not proof.
encompasses: Filter video-commerce sales tools to a realistic revenue band for the brand's size
Split video revenue from live-stream revenue and count video only
Read the sales graph shape before the product image, to avoid picking on looks
Pull the 180-day and multi-year graph, not just the recent spike
Check revenue spreads across several recent videos, not one old post
Require winning creative to already exist in the target market's language
Treat one platform's demand as a lead, not proof, for a different platform
Treat live ad run length as a funded test signal, not proof of profit
Read a high concurrent ad count as budget and confidence, then check revenue backs it up
inputs: web: TikTok Shop and native ad spy tools (public)
outputs: demand validation note with graph evidence and platform caveats
founder_sees: A short note on whether a trending product's demand is real or a platform fluke, with the evidence.

name: Scout ad libraries and competitor spend for new product candidates
what: Search public ad libraries and spy tools for products with real, sustained ad spend, and read what gap the incumbents leave, without copying any asset.
encompasses: Search ad libraries with generic offer and problem phrases, not brand names
Fall back to manual keyword search when a category filter returns nothing
Study established advertisers for the angle they leave open, not to copy them
Cap results per advertiser and widen the results window in spy tools
Rate each competitor's store and offer quality, not just the ad
Mine a validated competitor's top ad for avatar and angle in words only, never the asset
Scout native ad widgets for older-buyer problem categories
Never scrape an aggregator feed or copy a competitor's store outright
Train a fresh, time-boxed social account to see what it gets served
Grade competitor count with a green/amber/red ladder in the free and paid tools
inputs: web: Meta Ad Library, TikTok Ad Library (public, read-only)
outputs: competitor scouting sheet: advertiser, angle, store quality, gap found
tools: browser: headless chromium (public ad libraries only)
founder_sees: A list of competitor angles and the gap each one leaves, sourced from public ads only.

name: Run disciplined, time-boxed candidate research
what: Keep product research from sprawling: cap research time per candidate, delegate the repetitive search steps, and mine reviews for the price buyers say they would pay.
encompasses: Stop scrolling and log a candidate the moment it clears the basic screen
Require an easy on-camera demo or existing content before betting on a product
Track whether a seeded creator's post actually drove sales before calling it validated
Delegate research-heavy steps to an agent; keep go/no-go decisions with a person
Generate a long list of emotional sub-niches, then narrow to a working few
Treat AI-generated concepts and mockups as stimulus, not a sourcing spec
Mine reviews for the price buyers say they would actually pay
Re-check an AI-sourced brand's real revenue before treating ad volume as proof
Cross-check keyword volume and mentions against the ad library before shortlisting
founder_sees: A capped research log per candidate, with the price customers say they would pay.

name: Read trend direction, seasonality and competitive saturation together
what: Combine a multi-year trend line with how many sellers already exist, so a category is judged on real growth and real room, not on either signal alone.
encompasses: Run a 12-month and multi-year trend check on the exact sub-niche term
Widen category filters before abandoning a niche in a sales-data tool
Require search volume and unit sales to move together before trusting a spike
Estimate competitor revenue and apply a floor before treating them as proof
Treat missing traffic data as ambiguous, not proof a store is dead
Confirm the target buyer is reachable, online and shippable before sourcing
Count niche-level competitors and true substitutes, not just the exact product
Treat saturation as demand proof only with a concrete unserved angle
Treat a fragmented market with no leader as a possible opening, not proof on its own
Watch competitor density as an early sign a product's economics are shifting
Skip a product recognized as long-running from repeated personal exposure
inputs: web: Google Trends, category search data
outputs: trend and saturation memo with the graph and competitor count
founder_sees: A memo saying whether demand is growing, flat or a fad, and how crowded the space is.

name: Extend the product line and sharpen the differentiation angle
what: For a proven hero product, plan the next SKUs, and for any candidate, name the one thing that makes it different from the category's default, backed by an angle gap in the market.
encompasses: Build a brand around a proven product and add secondary products before it fades
List every angle competitors run, then name the avatar none of them serve
Prefer an angle that already holds a small but real share of ad volume
Rebuild the page and creative around a new avatar rather than bolt it on
Build an offer structure as a differentiation lever instead of copying the product
Use a branded or technical-sounding name only where the claim is provable
Change exactly one variable from the category's core expectation
Borrow design and mechanics from a distant industry, not a competitor
Name a self-interested and a feel-good reason to buy for every product
inputs: brand brain: hero SKU and avatar (once built)
outputs: differentiation brief with the named angle gap
founder_sees: A brief naming the one real difference a product has, and what it lets the brand say.

name: Classify demand pattern and plan cash around it
what: Tag every candidate evergreen, trending or seasonal, map its seasonal or gifting spikes, and check whether it truly earns a subscription or is a one-time novelty, before cash is committed.
encompasses: Classify every candidate evergreen or trending before spending
Map seasonality across several years and plan cash around it
Map gifting and occasion spikes the same way as holiday seasonality
Never commit MOQ inventory against a trend spike with no history
Check real replenishment rate before assuming a subscription model
Reject novelty products with no real recurring value
Judge whether a novelty creates repeat purchase or is a one-time sale
Weight lifetime value, not just AOV, for a low-ticket repeat item
founder_sees: A tag on each product (evergreen, seasonal, trend, subscription) with the cash timing it implies.

name: Model product economics and the compliance gate before funding a candidate
what: Price, margin, shipping, shelf-life and regulatory checks in one gate, in code, so a candidate cannot reach sourcing spend without a real margin and a clean compliance read.
encompasses: Reject a product priced too low to cover paid-acquisition cost, and gate on a dollar-margin floor and price-to-cost multiple together
Model markup at the low end, high end and future bulk cost of the price range
Re-quote the brand's own supplier cost instead of assuming a competitor's, and set price from a broad set of comparables
Separate a fixable execution problem from a structural cost problem
Price payment-gateway friction, real shipping cost, and return-to-origin or COD cost into the margin gate
Choose materials and packaging that survive parcel handling
Require shelf life to comfortably outlast time to market and sell
Check claim, labelling and registration rules, and any category-specific certification, per country before spend
Check delivery-window targets against chargeback risk
Check trademark and licensing exposure before listing a fandom-adjacent product
Launch with exactly one SKU and add variants only after proof
founder_sees: Pass or fail on margin and compliance, with the numbers computed in code, not guessed.

name: Translate specs, vet suppliers and log the research trail
what: Turn a validated concept into a structured sourcing request suppliers can quote against, and vet the supplier and the AI-sourced leads before spending real time on them.
encompasses: Write one structured sourcing request with MOQ, certifications and review strength, translating consumer language into manufacturing specification
Vet a shortlisted supplier with specific capability questions by phone, and verify an AI-surfaced supplier is reachable on the named platform
Order a small sample through the brand's own fulfilment chain before an MOQ order
Compare a private sourcing agent against marketplace-direct ordering on real numbers
Add custom branding and packaging only after the product is proven to sell
Set a reminder to re-quote every supplier as order volume grows
Price warranty and after-sales cost for a considered-purchase category
Keep a research log with a fixed set of columns for every candidate, and stop research at a validated product
Score expansion markets and re-check duty, VAT and creative localization before entering a new country
founder_sees: A structured sourcing request ready to send, plus a log of what was checked and why.

name: Score expansion markets and apply the go-live gates
what: Before a candidate goes live, run the remaining gates together: provable claims, an owned difference, brand-specific thresholds, contribution margin, and ad-cost headroom.
encompasses: Use founder excitement only as a tiebreaker between equally validated concepts
Try a change of presentation before concluding demand is absent, diagnosing ads and funnel before blaming the product
Run market-level questions before product-level ones, and score every validation question pass, caution or red flag
Run the full validation stack on every candidate regardless of source, and log every rule override with its justification
Require every product claim to be provable, and require a named owned difference, before a candidate reaches the shortlist
Replace default thresholds with the brand's own measured numbers
Gate on contribution margin after all real costs, not gross margin alone, and require positive ad-cost headroom
Check whether a recommendation source has a financial interest before trusting it
Build a staged offer ladder that lifts AOV without inventing claims
founder_sees: A pass/fail on every remaining launch gate, each with the number or evidence behind it.

name: Produce the scored shortlist and go/no-go memo for the founder
what: Rank the surviving candidates on a fixed scorecard and write the one-page memo the founder actually decides from, with a pre-set review date for whatever gets approved.
encompasses: Run a quick 10-point screen before spending research-tool time
Confirm every hard stop is clear before spending on samples or ads
Confirm the full research stack actually ran before greenlighting launch
Set a post-launch review date and metric before starting a test
Assign a named owner for post-test diagnosis before launch
Score every shortlisted candidate on five dimensions and rank before testing
Write a one-page go/no-go memo with evidence before any sourcing spend
Ask which warehouse or supply source gives the better-quality version
Test random un-niched products only to dodge high CPMs in brand-heavy verticals
Require at least one other seller already making money before copying a resale product
founder_sees: A ranked shortlist and a one-page memo asking for a yes, no or park decision.

name: Run field research discipline and hand validated angles to creative
what: Keep research grounded in real shopper behaviour and real time limits, then pass the validated avatar, hook and onboarding idea to the teams that build creative and the site.
encompasses: Hand the candidate avatar list to creative testing instead of testing avatars here
Screen a category for jargon it forces buyers to already know
Build a checkable origin story when the product itself cannot differ
Watch real shoppers in the aisle or on live search results
Run a time-boxed research-to-concept sprint, not open browsing
State the single sharpest reason a candidate differs, not a list
Measure and cut the time to a customer's first moment of delight
Give a small immediate payoff during an unavoidable wait
Name a brand from one emotional word, tested for instant recall
Confirm a new fulfilment app is a real shipping location pre-launch
Splice the brand's own validated hook into a longer new UGC body
outputs: avatar and angle handoff note to Paid creative and copy specialist
onboarding and naming notes to Brand strategist
founder_sees: A short handoff note telling the creative and brand teams which avatar and hook to build on.

name: Build tech packs, BOMs, packaging specs and product data records
what: Write the exact, versioned specification for every SKU: measurements with tolerances, a component-level bill of materials, packaging as its own cost line, and the physical claim checks that back the PDP.
encompasses: Write the spec in exact numbers with a tolerance band, not descriptive words
Write one versioned tech pack per SKU
Build a component-level bill of materials for the hero SKU first
Physically verify BOM lines and PDP material claims with the supplier
Send a physical reference sample with the tech pack to a new factory
Use the BOM to test an entry or premium version of a SKU
Quote retail packaging as its own line in the BOM
Build the missing BOM before any negotiation on a takeover or new client
Ask when COGS last declined on a mature SKU
Store tech packs and source files in the brand's own system, not the supplier's
inputs: brand brain: product records (specs, weights, materials, certifications)
trigger: event: new SKU or spec change
founder_sees: A versioned spec sheet and cost breakdown for every SKU, owned by the brand, not the supplier.

name: Discover and vet suppliers in India and overseas
what: Run supplier discovery as a funnel: broad platform search, message a wide shortlist, verify with a video call and certification check, and vet any sourcing agent the same way as a factory.
encompasses: Use Alibaba or similar platforms for research and shortlisting, not the final pick, on an ad-spend SKU
Message 10 to 15 factories and filter to verified suppliers with trade assurance
Video-call the shortlist to inspect the facility before trusting it
Require ISO or BSCI certification and drop a refusal
Keep at least one vetted backup factory for every SKU carrying ad spend
Get a direct contact channel with every supplier at first contact
Vet a sourcing agent with a sample, a direct channel and references before using them
Never buy or open a factory without a specific unmet quality gap
founder_sees: A shortlist of verified suppliers, each with a certification and verification status.

name: Draft RFQs and compare supplier quotes across volume tiers
what: Turn the spec into a structured RFQ, collect quotes on identical terms, and compare landed cost per unit and cash impact across volume tiers before picking a number.
encompasses: Get a factory-direct or manufacturer quote alongside any intermediary's
Request a structured quote and compare suppliers only on identical terms
Request quotes at several volume tiers and compare cash and cover, not just price
Treat the first quote as an opening position, not the final price
Use landed cost per unit, not the factory quote, as the pricing decision number
Confirm a SKU's margin is healthy on its own sell-through before a bulk order
Check the factory-direct versus intermediary price gap as a negotiation sanity check
outputs: quote comparison sheet with landed cost per tier
founder_sees: A quote comparison table with landed cost per unit and cash tied up, at each volume tier.

name: Run the 3-stage sample gate against a reference sample
what: No creative shoot, price or launch date before a sample from the exact factory clears a 3-stage gate against an approved reference kept both in-house and at the factory.
encompasses: Never shoot creative, set a price or commit a launch date before a sample from the exact factory
Run the 3-stage sample gate with a hard stop at the production sample
Score supplier communication and reliability during the sample stage
Keep one approved sample in-house and one at the factory as a reference
Compare each candidate's sample side by side against the approved reference
Never treat a passed sample as a guarantee of bulk quality
founder_sees: A clear stage status on every sample: passed, held or rejected, against the approved reference.

name: Negotiate cost-downs with backup-factory and benchmark leverage
what: Build real negotiating leverage before asking for a price break: a vetted alternate factory, a teardown of a competitor's product, and the category's normal factory margin.
encompasses: Test a cheaper competing supplier with a small, fully inspected batch first
Vet a real alternate factory before any cost-down negotiation
Buy and reverse-engineer competitor products before a cost-down negotiation
Learn the category's normal factory margin before negotiating
Choose a negotiation posture based on whether the relationship is strategic or replaceable
Frame a cost-down as a growth partnership, in units, not price talk
Write every price-break threshold and credit into the supplier agreement
Reconcile every invoice against the agreed price-break credits
Ask the factory to pass through its own sub-vendor volume breaks
Review the BOM with the supplier yearly and ask what unlocks the next price break
founder_sees: A negotiation brief with the concrete leverage found, before anyone talks price with the supplier.

name: Monitor commodity input costs and protect the supplier relationship
what: Track the priced-in raw materials behind a SKU on a set cadence, and know where a cost-down stops being worth the relationship risk.
encompasses: Pay a bit more for order-resize flexibility in a new SKU's first runs
Stop a cost-down before it triggers supplier retaliation
Monitor commodity-priced BOM inputs on a set cadence with multiple quotes
Benchmark component costs at category trade fairs
Consider buying a concentrated raw material directly at volume
Offer to share a specific cost with the supplier to make a negotiation two-sided
founder_sees: A monthly flag if a raw-material price has moved enough to change a SKU's cost.

name: Structure payment terms, float and MOQ cash planning, handed to Finance
what: Choose the payment route and terms per supplier relationship, and hand every float day, cash-locked figure and financing cost to Finance at each deal close, in the numbers Finance needs.
encompasses: Treat payment terms as float and push for longer terms as trust grows
Default to trade-assurance-style protected payment for a new or unproven supplier
Allow direct transfer only for a proven supplier, with owner sign-off, for a real discount
Tie the balance payment to a passed pre-shipment QC report
Ask about consignment where the product has resale or reclaim value
Ask for a hybrid payment cadence with a buffer for the brand's own ordering mistakes
Ask if the supplier uses export credit insurance or invoice factoring to extend terms
Make financing cost an explicit BOM line and negotiate the split
Structure a partner-financed bulk buy for a cash-capped recurring SKU
Hand float days, cash locked and financing cost to Finance at each close
founder_sees: A cash-and-MOQ packet for Finance: float days, cash locked, and financing cost, per deal.

name: Run pre-shipment inspection and defect disposition
what: Book third-party inspection before a container leaves, size the defect buffer from real history, and record every disposition decision on defective units.
encompasses: Book a mandatory third-party pre-shipment inspection before the container leaves
Size the order's defect buffer from the observed defect rate
Decide and record whether to return or absorb defective units
Run a written QC checklist before every production run ships
Split customer returns into supplier-fault and fit/expectation buckets
Reconcile receiving counts and defects against the inspection report on arrival
founder_sees: An inspection report and a stated decision on any defective units, before goods ship.

name: Choose freight mode and 3PL and manage cross-border logistics
what: Pick air, sea or a hybrid by weight, launch date and cash cover, select a 3PL on service history rather than lowest quote, and check cross-border thresholds before committing a lane.
encompasses: Choose freight mode by weight, volume and the launch calendar
Hybridize freight: air a small first batch, then sea-restock
Start planning the next shipment the day the current one lands
Order heavy or bulky items early enough for sea freight
Choose a freight forwarder on service and reliability, not the lowest quote
Verify a recommended cross-border 3PL independently before switching lanes
Check the customs de minimis threshold before choosing a cross-border DTC lane
Match freight mode and terms to the store type: slow freight for luxury, fast for impulse
Choose a 3PL on documented accuracy, speed, communication and Q4 surge history
Visit a candidate 3PL's warehouse in person before signing
Ask a candidate 3PL how it handles returns, damages and restocks
Track 3PL inventory turnover weekly and hold a monthly review
founder_sees: A freight and 3PL recommendation, with the service history behind the pick.

name: Compute reorder points, safety stock and demand plans per SKU
what: Calculate, in code, a reorder point and safety stock for every SKU from its own velocity, lead time and spike risk, and size non-routine orders from the committed channel push, not trailing sales alone.
encompasses: Set a computed reorder point per SKU from velocity, lead time and safety stock
Run a named weekly review of velocity, lead time and stock position
Size safety stock from the brand's own spike and delay risk
Send suppliers the sales forecast before problems appear
Write a demand plan before any non-routine purchase order
Size a non-routine order from the committed channel push, not trailing velocity alone
Put every required field in the PO draft so nothing is left to the factory
Flag a below-reorder-point SKU on the PDP and throttle its ad spend
Size a subscription SKU's reorder point from committed cadence, not trailing sales
Build the demand plan from bundle sell-through, not single-unit history
Round the order quantity up to the supplier's carton or MOQ multiple
founder_sees: A reorder point and a ready-to-send PO draft for every SKU nearing its threshold, computed in code.

name: Flag supplier and country concentration risk and refresh landed cost
what: Compute supplier and country concentration shares, keep a mapped backup in a second country, and recompute landed cost the moment price, freight, FX or duty changes.
encompasses: Compute and flag supplier concentration share
Compute and flag country concentration share
Map a backup factory in a second country before it's needed
Score a candidate sourcing country on 4 qualitative factors
Run the lead-time versus cost trade-off with real quotes before moving production
Hold volume flat and ask for a concession when a shock breaks margin
Weigh a cost-down push against a CAC push using the real BOM
Decide whether a full component BOM is worth building given the SKU's COGS size
Recompute landed cost whenever price, freight, FX or duty changes
founder_sees: A flag when one supplier or country carries too much of the brand's volume, and a fresh landed cost.

name: Run onboarding sourcing audits and automate PO cadence at scale
what: In week one of a takeover or new brand, audit the whole sourcing base once; at high SKU count, move purchase orders from a weekly to a daily cadence.
encompasses: Run a full sourcing audit in the first week of a takeover or new client
Automate purchase orders from weekly to daily at high SKU count
Base a sourcing operator near key suppliers to build terms faster
Open a new market with one cross-border 3PL hub and one global ad set
Re-quote competing factories on a schedule even for a happy supplier
Check IP and trademark exposure before reverse engineering a reference sample
Use an easy-iteration location to test, then move scaled production to a hub
Hire a freelance designer to build the tech pack when design skill is missing
Order pre-production samples across the size range to confirm grading
Use a general AI checklist to draft the landed cost category list, then verify by hand
Ask an established supplier for a premium courier upgrade on a large order
founder_sees: A one-time full audit of every supplier and SKU when a brand or account is taken over.

name: Hand sourcing and ops hiring needs to Money and Ops
what: When sourcing volume outgrows the current team, draft the role scorecard and hand the hiring process to the Money and Ops specialist rather than running it here.
encompasses: Run a five-step hiring sequence from scorecard to reference-checked offer
Write a role scorecard that names required outcomes and irrelevant traits
Use standardized screening questions to pre-filter and flag deep-dive topics
Run a chronological interview to catch inflated titles
Test finalist hires with a trapped case study and a culture questionnaire
Hire a specialized role in a lower-cost hub instead of a local generalist
Keep the store's proven marketing edge in-house below a revenue threshold
Run a deliberately lean headcount and add a role only at capacity
Run a daily task and time-log channel with every direct report
Give management feedback on a predictable daily cadence, not at random
outputs: role scorecard draft for a sourcing or ops hire
handoff note to Money and Ops
founder_sees: A draft scorecard for a sourcing hire, handed to Money and Ops to run the actual hiring process.

name: Hand cash, margin and deal-risk signals to Finance and the founder
what: Surface the sourcing-side numbers Finance and the founder need for cash discipline and any recovery or capability decision, without doing Finance's own P&L work here.
encompasses: Build a daily color-coded P&L digest with a required miss explanation
Close the books monthly and pay out from free cash, not EBITDA
Use a five-slide accountability deck to negotiate a way out of a cash hole
Screen a founder's character with mutual reference calls before a deal
Evaluate an internal sourcing capability as a picks-and-shovels product for other brands
outputs: sourcing-side numbers packet for Finance's P&L and cash model
founder_sees: A packet of sourcing-side cash and margin numbers, handed to Finance and the founder.

name: Flag slow-moving and dead stock and draft a clearance plan
what: Watch inventory age against velocity across DTC and marketplace stock, flag a SKU before it becomes dead weight, and draft a markdown, bundle or discontinue plan with the cash impact.
encompasses: Compute days-of-stock and sell-through velocity per SKU across channels
Flag a SKU approaching the long-term storage or dead-stock threshold
Draft a markdown, bundle-out or discontinue option with the cash recovered
Recommend discontinuing a SKU whose demand pattern is a one-time novelty
Route a dead-stock decision to the founder with the write-off amount
inputs: warehouse: inventory age and velocity by channel
founder_sees: An alert on stock that is going dead, with a clearance plan and the cash it would recover or lose.

name: Set up and verify the Amazon seller account without compliance risk
what: Get the Amazon account, entity, payout and identity verification right the first time, since a rejected or later-flagged account costs weeks.
encompasses: Decide FBA vs FBM, and confirm the product is the brand's own, before opening the account
Gate adding Amazon on the brand's own landed cost and price, not on course figures, with a launch budget built from line items
Match the target revenue band to the cash the brand actually has available
Set a launch date once price, margin and differentiation clear; stop re-researching
Reject a product that cannot win a price or review fight against the top 10 listings
Model Seller Fulfilled Prime as an FBM alternative, and choose the Professional plan above about 40 units a month expected
Disclose any existing or previously suspended account before opening a new one
Gather the full identity, bank and tax document set, name matching ID exactly, and use a business credit card at signup
Prepare for the live video identity verification call with matching documents
Do not change bank details or business address for 1 to 2 months after approval
Open the account under a business entity with its own EIN and bank account
Buy UPC barcodes from GS1 directly, never from gray-market resellers
inputs: brand brain: entity and product records
founder_sees: A go/no-go memo on adding Amazon, with the account and document checklist ready.

name: File trademark, enrol Brand Registry and protect brand equity
what: Sequence the trademark filing, listing creation and Brand Registry enrolment correctly, then turn on the Storefront and Subscribe & Save benefits it unlocks.
encompasses: Add VAT to the fee lines before judging margin on UK or EU sales
File a trademark application before or at listing creation, do not wait for approval
Choose a design mark over a word mark when the brand name sits on the listing image
Create the listing before applying for Brand Registry, since enrolment needs an ASIN
Record the trademark serial number in the brand record right after filing
Enrol in Brand Registry as soon as eligible and turn on its benefits
Track the Brand Referral Bonus with tracked links; do not assume a fixed percentage
Get a lawyer-reviewed NNN agreement before a production PO to an overseas factory
Enrol a repeat-purchase product in Subscribe & Save once Brand Registered
Build a Brand Registry Storefront as a destination for off-Amazon traffic
founder_sees: A checklist confirming trademark filed, Brand Registry enrolled and Storefront live, in the right order.

name: Screen Amazon product candidates for price, competition and demand pattern
what: Apply Amazon-specific elimination screens before a candidate reaches sourcing: price floor, page-1 price spread, keyword variability, brand dominance and a real fad filter.
encompasses: Screen out disqualifying products first: cheap, head-on competitive, seasonal or restricted
Target a sell price of $25 or more for a new launch; treat $15 as the floor
Require both real demand and low competition before shortlisting
Reject categories dominated by 1 or 2 legacy brands
Reject a product with a tight page-1 price cluster; prefer a wide legitimate spread
Prefer products with many distinct search phrasings over one or two monolithic terms
Require at least 8 months of listing age on comparable products before treating demand as evergreen
inputs: web: Amazon best-seller and category browse pages (public)
founder_sees: A pass/fail screen for a candidate against Amazon's own price and competition patterns.

name: Mine competitor reviews and keywords for Amazon opportunity
what: Read 1 to 3 star reviews on competing listings for fixable complaints, confirm mid-rated high-volume sellers as a demand-and-gap signal, and mine keywords from reverse-ASIN and autocomplete sources.
encompasses: Mine 1-star to 3-star reviews of selling competitors and write each fixable complaint into the product brief
Treat a 4.1 to 4.3 star competitor doing meaningful monthly revenue as demand proof with a spec gap
Run two different research-filter recipes as separate passes, not one copied verbatim
Validate a keyword gap live on Amazon search, not only inside the research tool
Cross-check any tool revenue estimate against BSR and a sales estimator before trusting it
Use giftability as a tie-breaker only, never as a gate
Run reverse-ASIN keyword research on 2 to 3 competitor ASINs
Cross-check Amazon autocomplete suggestions against revenue data
founder_sees: A list of fixable complaints from real reviews, and keywords competitors are missing.

name: Model Amazon channel economics and the margin gate
what: Model the full Amazon fee stack, storage cost, PPC budget and price-parity rule against DTC, in code, so a SKU only launches with a real net margin after every fee.
encompasses: Set a 30% or higher net margin gate after landed cost and all Amazon fees
Price at 3x or more the unit manufacturing cost, consider premium positioning
Model the full Amazon fee stack line by line before committing to stock
Compute monthly storage cost from cubic feet and the live per-cubic-foot rate
Design packaging to the smallest FBA size tier that still protects the product
Read the monthly Amazon P&L by fee line, never by revenue alone
Audit fee charges and lost or damaged inventory claims every month
Set the PPC budget from cost per click, conversion rate and margin, with a launch reserve
Keep the Amazon price at or above the brand's own DTC price unless deliberately modelled
Use Amazon's coupons, Lightning Deals and Prime Day, but never below the margin gate
Set the negative-keyword spend threshold from the brand's own margin
Enrol a qualifying low-price, lightweight SKU in Small and Light to cut the FBA fee
outputs: monthly Amazon P&L by fee line
founder_sees: A monthly Amazon P&L by fee line, and the net margin after every fee, computed in code.

name: Manage Amazon-bound sourcing, sample approval and pre-shipment inspection
what: Run the sourcing steps specific to an FBA-bound production run: capacity check, printed sample sign-off, inspection with a barcode scan, and FNSKU labelling at the factory.
encompasses: Confirm a factory's maximum monthly output before setting a launch date
Pay for a printed sample and approve it against the product brief before the FBA-bound run
Run a third-party inspection, including a barcode scan, before releasing the balance payment
Pay new Amazon-bound suppliers by a reversible method until trust is established
Print the FNSKU barcode on the packaging at the factory, never let Amazon apply the label
Choose air or sea freight against the launch date and PPC budget already committed
Source consumable or ingested products domestically unless the overseas path is confirmed
founder_sees: A confirmed sample, inspection and correct labelling before goods ship into FBA.

name: Build and optimise the Amazon listing
what: Write and structure the listing so the target keyword sits where Amazon's search ranks on, every image slot earns its place, and every attribute field is filled.
encompasses: Put the number one target keyword in the first 2 words of the title and the first bullet
Sort keywords into core, supporting and buzzwords-to-cut, mining adjacent listings for extra attribute terms
Write 5 bullets that lead with a benefit and carry one true, specific claim each
Make the main image differentiate the product on the search grid, and use every secondary image slot including a comparison chart
Fill every attribute field correctly, especially shelf life and units per sellable unit
Fill backend search terms with leftover true keywords not already visible
Set a future offer start date so launch traffic never lands on an out-of-stock listing
Build a new listing for an own-brand product; join an existing ASIN only if resellers already listed it
Plan buffer time for compliance flags on supplements, diet claims or anything a scanner may misread
Use A+ content and a listing or index checker once Brand Registered
Choose a specific, accurate category node instead of a too-generic auto-suggestion
Use Amazon's AI listing generator from an existing DTC product page instead of a blank listing
inputs: brand brain: product copy and claims tiers
outputs: Amazon listing draft (title, bullets, images brief, attributes, backend keywords)
founder_sees: A complete draft Amazon listing, ready for a human to paste into Seller Central.

name: Prepare and ship FBA inbound shipments correctly
what: Build the shipment from measured case dimensions against FBA's hard limits, reuse a saved template, and keep every paper trail so a lost-inventory claim can be filed.
encompasses: Build every shipment from measured case dimensions and weight against the hard FBA size limits
Save a case-pack template after the first shipment so repeat shipments reuse the same counts
Check every box label against the carrier label before dispatch
Always use the true ship-from address on every FBA shipment
Use small parcel for boxes and LTL pallets for larger volumes
Keep every carrier receipt and bill of lading before handover
Book the carrier collection; a tracking number alone does not finish a shipment
Read the FBA Inventory Breakdown before assuming stock is lost; escalate only past the normal window
Answer every dangerous-goods and prep question accurately, and set the right prep category
founder_sees: A shipment plan that fits FBA's size limits and a full paper trail if a claim is needed later.

name: Plan and protect an Amazon product launch
what: Concentrate real demand into the first weeks with stock and PPC live together, build an audience before launch day, and protect a novel product against copycats from day one.
encompasses: Concentrate genuine sales into launch day and the first weeks, with stock live and PPC on
Build an audience (waitlist, social, seeded creators) before launch day, not after
Launch one SKU first; add colour or size variants only when the category requires them
Use only compliant launch levers; drop manual review generation from the plan
Use price as an inventory throttle only when selling faster than the next delivery can restock
Recover a stalled launch by reading sessions and unit session percentage before re-testing
Route Amazon buyers to email or DTC with a packaging insert or QR code, no review ask
Protect a novel product with Brand Registry, Transparency and IP filing, not launch speed alone
founder_sees: A launch week plan that lines up stock, PPC and audience together, plus a copycat-protection checklist.

name: Build the Amazon PPC campaign structure and hand off to Media buyer
what: Draft the automatic-to-manual PPC campaign structure, negative-keyword hygiene and retargeting layer as a change list, and hand execution to the Media buyer specialist since ad-account writes sit there.
encompasses: Run an automatic campaign first to discover converting search terms
Split the automatic campaign into 4 ad groups by targeting type with separate bids
Build manual keyword campaigns from proven search terms after 2 to 4 weeks of data
Run product targeting on weaker or higher-priced competitor ASINs, one ad group per competitor
Add negative keywords to every live campaign from day one
Judge PPC on net profit, not sales, and test reducing budget once organic momentum exists
Diagnose an ineligible-to-advertise listing by isolating the trigger
Add Sponsored Display or DSP retargeting once Sponsored Products is proven
outputs: PPC campaign structure change list, handed to Media buyer
founder_sees: A ready-to-run Amazon PPC structure, handed to the Media buyer to execute.

name: Manage marketplace reviews, feedback and policy/account-health compliance
what: Request reviews only through permitted paths, contest misplaced feedback, and watch Account Health weekly so a policy notice never becomes a surprise suspension.
encompasses: Request reviews only through Amazon's permitted request path, never selecting only satisfied buyers
Never reimburse, gift or recruit friends or family for reviews, or link a refund to a review change
Use Vine only under current terms and only once the product is genuinely ready
Contest seller feedback that is really a product review within the window, without offering a benefit
Watch Account Health weekly for order defect rate, claims and policy notices
Run a full policy compliance audit covering barcodes, ship-from address, accounts and shared devices
Monitor Brand Registry alerts for hijackers and open a case immediately
Assign a named human owner for every account-changing action
founder_sees: A weekly Account Health check and an immediate flag if a hijacker or policy notice appears.

name: Manage Amazon inventory: replenishment, aged stock and IPI limits
what: Size replenishment shipments from real cover targets, treat a stockout as the failure mode to avoid, and watch IPI and storage limits live so a restock is never blocked.
encompasses: Send 3 to 6 months of stock cover per inbound shipment, smaller for an unproven SKU
Treat a stockout as the failure mode to avoid; reorder early and rush if velocity rises
Watch inventory age and act before the long-term storage threshold hits
Plan Q4 stock early, accounting for about 3x normal volume and slower check-in
Fetch current IPI, storage and restock limits live before planning inventory
Use the Restock Inventory widget's days-of-supply estimate as a starting point, not the final answer
Flag inventory approaching 150 days as an early warning before the long-term storage threshold
founder_sees: A replenishment plan and an early warning before FBA stock goes into long-term storage.

name: Diagnose Amazon sales changes and run compliant native promotions
what: Split a sales change into traffic versus conversion before acting on it, check attribution and seasonality before calling a product a failure, and use only Amazon's own compliant promotion tools.
encompasses: Read sessions and unit session percentage separately before diagnosing a sales change
Track off-Amazon ad attribution before trusting its reported return
Map revenue by month for a full year before calling a product a failure
Use Amazon's own coupons, Lightning Deals and Prime Day, but never below the margin gate
founder_sees: A diagnosis saying whether a sales drop is a traffic problem or a conversion problem, with the numbers.

name: Plan Amazon portfolio growth and channel decisions
what: Decide when to add a second SKU, delegate non-revenue admin, and write the one-page memo behind any decision to add or expand the Amazon channel.
encompasses: Add a second ASIN only once the first hero SKU has proven sell-through and cleared the margin gate
Master a task before outsourcing it, but delegate non-revenue admin work early
Delay buying paid Amazon tools until there is enough sales data for them to act on
Set a growth or planned-decline target once a revenue goal is hit
Account for about 2 months of manufacturing and freight lead time when judging a trending product
Write a one-page Amazon channel decision memo before adding the channel
founder_sees: A one-page memo on whether and when to expand the Amazon channel or add a SKU.

name: Source alternative financing and manufacturers for a hard-to-source launch
what: When a product is hard to source or fund, widen the search to crowdfunding, private capital, manufacturer referrals and mass outreach, and prototype cheaply before committing.
encompasses: Fund the first production run with a pre-order crowdfunding campaign, not personal capital
Ask a manufacturer for a referral to cover a production step they cannot do themselves
Run a tracked, mass cold-outreach campaign to 50 or more manufacturers for a hard-to-source product
Ask a manufacturer making an adjacent product for a free leftover sample to prototype cheaply
Widen manufacturer search to supplier databases, trade shows, directories and agents when a single platform stalls
Negotiate manufacturer price with a volume-commitment quote and by citing a competing offer
Ask the manufacturer to execute design changes before hiring a separate CAD designer
Commission a factory audit or a sourcing-agent visit before a large order with an unfamiliar manufacturer
Fund the first production run with a private investor for repayment plus a profit share
founder_sees: A financing and sourcing memo when the normal supplier or capital path has stalled.

name: Run Amazon growth experiments and channel tests
what: Test the smaller, situational Amazon growth levers, each with a defined read: converting FBM to FBA, a Small and Light enrolment, a design-vendor bake-off, an Amazon Live stream, and affiliate-link recapture.
encompasses: Test converting an existing FBM SKU to FBA and measure the sales change from Prime eligibility
Ship the first production run to yourself first for a personal quality check before forwarding to Amazon
Test the same logo brief across several design-sourcing price tiers before picking a designer
Run an Amazon Live stream demonstrating the product around launch day
Use the brand's own Amazon Associates link on its own external traffic to recapture the affiliate commission
founder_sees: A short test brief for each smaller Amazon growth lever, with what it should move.

name: Create and optimise listings on Flipkart, Myntra and Nykaa
what: Build and keep current the brand's listings on India's other major marketplaces, adapting the title, bullet and image rules each platform enforces, since none of them are Amazon.
encompasses: Complete each platform's seller onboarding and category-approval process
Match image and copy specs to each marketplace's own guide
Localize title and bullet structure to the platform's own search ranking signals
Fill every mandatory attribute field the category requires
Keep GST-compliant invoicing and category eligibility current
Track approval status and reasons for any listing rejection
inputs: brand brain: product records and claims tiers
trigger: event: new marketplace listing or refresh
founder_sees: A ready-to-submit listing for Flipkart, Myntra or Nykaa, matching that platform's own rules.

name: Check BIS, hallmarking and labelling compliance for marketplace listings
what: Before any jewellery, textile or regulated listing goes live, confirm the BIS, hallmarking and labelling requirements are met and recorded, since a marketplace can pull a listing or a buyer can flag it.
encompasses: Confirm BIS hallmark, karatage and HUID are present and recorded for gold jewellery
Check textile labelling rules (fibre content, care, origin) before listing
Confirm the marketplace's own category-review requirements are met (Nykaa, Myntra)
Keep certification documents attached to the product data record
Flag a listing that lacks a required certificate before it goes live
inputs: brand brain: product records and certifications
web: BIS and marketplace category rules (public)
trigger: event: new listing or certification renewal
founder_sees: A pass/fail on BIS, hallmarking and labelling compliance before a regulated listing goes live.

name: Monitor Buy Box ownership, reseller pricing and MAP violations
what: Watch who holds the Buy Box and what unauthorised resellers are charging across marketplaces, and flag a MAP or price-integrity problem for the founder rather than changing any price.
encompasses: Check Buy Box ownership on the brand's own ASINs and listings
Scan for unauthorised resellers on the exact listing
Compare reseller price against the brand's own MAP and DTC price
Flag a price or Buy Box loss with the evidence, never adjust price directly
Track whether Sponsored Product ads are funding an unauthorised reseller's sales
inputs: brand brain: MAP and DTC price
outputs: Buy Box and reseller pricing report
founder_sees: A weekly report on who holds the Buy Box and any reseller undercutting the brand's own price.

name: Build and hand off marketplace catalogue feeds
what: Keep one clean product feed (titles, images, prices, availability, GTIN) that Media buyer and Organic can plug into shopping ads and marketplace channels, so nobody re-types product data by hand.
encompasses: Maintain a master product feed with accurate price, stock and image fields
Map brand product data to each marketplace's and each ad platform's feed schema
Flag a feed field that is missing or stale before it reaches an ad platform
Hand the validated feed to Media buyer for catalogue and dynamic ads
Hand the validated feed to Organic and search for shopping-feed structured data
founder_sees: A single, current product feed, validated and handed to Media buyer and Organic to plug in.
